function: above_phy: learned QMIX only selects each UD channel access mode; beamforming, RIS phase shifts, and time allocation come from alternating optimization, not learning (pp. 6-7).
notes: Excluded as above_phy. The only learned component is the attention-enhanced QMIX that picks each UD access mode among energy harvesting, RIS-assisted relaying, NOMA, and backscatter (p. 7: "we focus on optimizing the access mode X"; p. 7: "Apart from the binary access mode selection, the other" variables go to the inner-loop optimization). Fig. 2 (p. 6) shows the inner loop fixing X and solving BS beamforming, RIS phase shifts, and time allocation with the AO method (p. 8: "solved by the AO method alternately", with SCA, SDR, and CVX, pp. 9-10; Algorithm 1), so no learned method produces the beams or the RIS phase shifts of area 3. The mode flags (RIS on or off, NOMA on or off, harvesting) are channel access choices, as the paper calls them. If the reviewer reads the optimized part as the only physical-layer function, no_learning would apply instead.
